Gold Rush. The trainees find a gold nugget and dream of ways to spend their riches.

Fire Engine. Bing doesn't get to sit in the fire engine but later gets to help out when Arlo is stuck.

Phoney. After a big day, everyone wants to sit back and listen to some relaxing music.

Honey Badger. A honey badger claims a watering hole, so Kwazii challenges her to a digging contest.

Fairy in the Attic! Rebecca and Murphi make a house and a box dragon, but will they solve the dust mystery?
Dance Away. It's the nursery dance, but Ava feels she can't dance like everyone else.

Noisy Neighbours. The builders are so noisy that the gang can't hear themselves play their instruments!
Music. After finding some pasta, the Froglets create a rock band with maracas, a drum and a saxophone.

Moss. Birdwatcher George shows the Fact Pack how moss grows and helps wildlife.

The Song of the Garden. Yukee's bouncing ball sets off a musical chain of events without anyone saying a word!

Brother from the Same Planet: When Homer is late picking up Bart from a school football game, Bart gets a surrogate dad from an agency.
I Love Lisa: On Valentine's Day, Lisa takes pity on Ralph and gives him a card. But when he falls in love with her, it leads to a bitter feud between their families.
Duffless: Homer fails a breathalyser test while driving home from the Duff brewery and has to quit drinking for a month.
Last Exit to Springfield: Homer takes on Mr Burns in a labour struggle that rapidly spirals out of control after Homer leads the workers on strike.
The stars of It's A Sin join Paul Hollywood, Prue Leith, Matt Lucas and Noel Fielding to celebrate Christmas. And the London Community Gospel Choir perform All I Want for Christmas.
On the Christmas box: Michael McIntyre's Christmas Wheel, First Dates at Christmas, Strictly the Real Full Monty, Love Actually, World's Strongest Man, Elves, and No Time to Die.
This time on the 'Box: Adolescence, 99 to Beat, Coronation Street, David Blaine: Do Not Attempt, Big Night of Musicals by The National Lottery and Building Britain's Superhomes.
This time it's Adolescence, Tribe with Bruce Parry, and Bad Dog Academy. Also Tempting Fortune, The Yorkshire Vet, and Million Dollar Secret.
In this special Valentine's episode, Mayfair-based Miki is looking for a man to treat her like a princess. Meanwhile, self-confessed nerd Sam just wants Daenerys from Game of Thrones.
Is there chemistry between hunky scientist Ashley and single parent Sonia? Burlesque dancer Becky meets budding comedian Lewis. Do Queen fans Gemma and Paolo have a kind of magic?
This time on the 'Box: Adolescence, 99 to Beat, Coronation Street, David Blaine: Do Not Attempt, Big Night of Musicals by The National Lottery and Building Britain's Superhomes.
This time it's Adolescence, Tribe with Bruce Parry, and Bad Dog Academy. Also Tempting Fortune, The Yorkshire Vet, and Million Dollar Secret.
Barefoot Bob's: Gordon visits Barefoot Bob's beachside restaurant in Massachusetts, where husband and wife Marc and Lisa struggle to attract customers during the winter months.
The Big Ibizan Zoo One: How will party fanatic Sonny's bride Jazmin greet his plans for a zoo-themed Ibizan beach party wedding with everyone covered in animal-print body paint?
Kathleen-Angel suffers heartbreak alone in the woods, and concern grows when she fails to return home. Meanwhile, Theresa is forced to confess when her lies catch up with her.
The Sk8er Boi One: Will Andy's plans for a skater-themed wedding make his bride Bobby's wheels spin? Or will there be broken bones and broken hearts on the big day?
(2018) Feel-good British family comedy. Sarah's (Beattie Edmondson) chaotic life gets even more complicated when she inherits a naughty pug from her nan.
Mill Street Bistro (Part 1/2): The owner of the Mill Street Bistro in Ohio claims to have the best menu between New York and LA. But the diners don't agree.
Mill Street Bistro (Part 2/2): In the conclusion to the Mill Street Bistro saga, Gordon's disagreement with the proprietor erupts into one of his most intense confrontations yet.
The Final: The finalists make citrus celebration cakes, crème brûlée doughnuts and a tribute to iconic British landscapes. Who'll be the zest and be crowned the series winner?
(1997) Comedy sequel starring Alex D. Linz as a resourceful boy who's stranded at home with chickenpox when a top-secret military microchip comes his way. Can he keep it safe from crooks?
So It Has Come to This: A Simpsons Clip Show: Bart's special April Fools' Day prank seriously misfires when the whole house explodes.
The Front: At his high school reunion, Homer wins several awards, including 'Most Weight Gained' and 'Most Improved Odour'. But then the Principal finds out he never graduated.
Whacking Day: Lisa asks singer Barry White to help stop the cruel Springfield 'Whacking Day' tradition of hitting snakes with sticks.
Krusty Gets Cancelled: When Krusty's show gets axed, Bart and Lisa enlist Bette Midler, Hugh Hefner, the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Elizabeth Taylor to help him get it back.
Homer's Barbershop Quartet: Homer reminisces about the Be Sharps, the barbershop quartet he was in with Barney, Apu and Principal Skinner. Guest starring George Harrison.
Homr: When Homer loses all the family's money with an unwise investment, he becomes a human guinea pig to earn some cash - and that's when he becomes extremely intelligent...
Pokey Mom: Marge notices a prison inmate's artistic talent and helps him to get a job painting a mural at the school. But he clashes with Skinner. Michael Keaton guest stars.

p.d: Paul, Prue, Matt and Noel celebrate New Year with Kim-Joy and Jon from Bake Off 2018 and Hermine and Rowan from the 2020 Bake Off bubble, who compete in three seasonal challenges.
Brand new series: Brittany and Ben head to St Mary's for an induced birth. And Clementine and Olumide prepare to welcome their second baby together.
(2022) High octane, Shinkansen-set comedy thriller starring Brad Pitt. A jaded assassin does one last job on a villain-packed train.

The Empire Builders: The railroad is coming to Walnut Grove, and with it the promise of jobs and economic growth. But that joy turns sour when the townspeople learn the side effects.
Love: Laura's childhood friend falls in love with Mr Edwards. She doesn't seem to mind the age difference, but Mr Edwards finds it tough.
Alden's Dilemma: Mr Edwards is suspicious of a young, handsome minister sent to Walnut Grove by the diocese, and Reverend Alden feels his position is threatened.
Marvin's Garden: Jenny nearly drowns looking for a locket in the lake. Dr Marvin convinces Laura to let Jenny help with his garden to rehabilitate. She turns out to be his last patient.
Sins Of The Fathers: Sarah Carter's imposing father visits Walnut Grove, demanding they move back to New York. He tries to 'buy' the boys' affection, but Sarah doesn't rise to it.
The Older Brothers: The Younger Brothers haven't been out of prison very long when they decide to hold Mr Edwards for ransom.
Hawkeye: Hawkeye is rescued by a Korean family when he is injured in a jeep accident. He knows how dangerous it can be to fall asleep with a concussion, so he talks to the family non-stop.
Some 38th Parallels: Frank becomes increasingly paranoid that the locals are stealing the camp's garbage, so he decides to auction off 150 pounds of it.
The Novocaine Mutiny: Frank charges Hawkeye with mutiny, but they each have different views of the circumstances leading to the court-martial.
Smilin' Jack: A helicopter pilot wants to get back to fighting despite his failing health while a soldier who received two Purple Hearts is tired of the bloodbath and wishes to be sent home.
Whicher is hired by a powerful political grandee to investigate violent threats made against his son, who has recently returned from India with his young family.

Tá Lola ag ceapadh nach bhfuil Charlie agus Marv mór le chéile níos mó. (Lola is convinced that Charlie and Marv are not friends anymore.)

Tá Mó in ann na píosaí leadránacha den chlár teilifíse is fearr leis a scipeáil. (Mo uses a power to skip the boring bits of his favourite TV show.)

Féachann Zak le bronntanas deas a fháil dá athair ar Lá na nAithreacha. (Zak wants to get a nice gift for his father for Father's Day.)

Goideann Mó cos chré Selina. (Mo steals Selina's clay foot.)

Molann Jake agus Marceline do Finn an Banphrionsa Guma a thabhairt amach ar choinne. (Jake and Marceline both give Finn advice for asking Princess Bubblegum on a date.)
Caithfidh Pat teacht i gcabhair ar Chaipín, a d'éalaigh le bróiste mháthair Lola. (Pat has to rescue Caipín, who has run off with Lola's mother's brooch.)

The Locomotion Interruption. Amy and Leonard take a road trip, Penny has an interview at Bernadette's company, and Howard has issues with Stuart's relationship with his mum. S8, Ep1
The Junior Professor Solution. Howard signs up to take Sheldon's class, and tensions between Penny and Bernadette give Amy an opportunity to play one against the other. S8, Ep2
The First Pitch Insufficiency. NASA asks Wolowitz to throw the first pitch at an Angels baseball game. And Sheldon says that he and Amy are a better couple than Leonard and Penny. S8, Ep3
The Hook-Up Reverberation. Raj's girlfriend gives Penny the cold shoulder after he tells her about their history, and the guys consider buying into Stuart's comic-book emporium. S8, Ep4
The Focus Attenuation. Amy and Bernadette accuse Penny of becoming a party pooper. And the guys brainstorm about inventing something cool. S8, Ep5
The Expedition Approximation. Sheldon and Raj go on an expedition that turns into a test of how long before they get under each other's skin. Leonard and Penny argue about money. S8, Ep6
Misinterpretation Agitation. Penny's sales pitch leaves a doctor-client smitten and the guys help her deal with it, and Bernadette and Amy debate female scientists and sexuality. S8, Ep7
The Prom Equivalency. Amy and Bernadette organise a prom to be held atop the guys' apartment complex, but Sheldon is leery of all the prom pomp, circumstance and romancing. S8, Ep8
The Septum Deviation. Leonard needs surgery for a deviated septum, and Sheldon feels an operation is too dangerous and that his roommate may not make it out alive. S8, Ep9
The Champagne Reflection. Sheldon bids farewell to his Fun With Flags podcast. Leonard, Howard and Raj probe a late professor's research in search of some hidden significance. S8, Ep10
The Clean Room Infiltration. Amy plans a Victorian dinner for Christmas Eve, while Raj, Leonard and Howard try to remove a pigeon that flew into the clean room at the university. S8, Ep11
Sleepless In Steatocystoma. Jen has growths on her ears that cause her depression, pain and vertigo. Plus, Juliet is in distress because of the bumps all over her neck and chest. S2, Ep7
Dr. Lee Nose Best! Tony has large growths on his nose that impair his breathing. Can Dr. Lee help? And, Marie has an unsightly lump on her forehead that makes her a hermit. S2, Ep9
peh-DUN-kyo-LAY-ted. Traci's confidence was destroyed after years of bullying about the bumps that have plagued her face for 20 years. Ravon has a unique dangling growth on his leg. S2, Ep11
Booty And The Beach. Eric hopes Dr. Lee can remove the giant growth from his backside. Plus, Michael makes jokes, but he knows the bump on his head is anything but funny. S4, Ep11
Alligator Arms. Robert has thousands of unique bumps on his arms that Dr. Lee has never seen. Stuart's cluster of back bumps disgusts his wife but thrills Dr. Lee. S4, Ep12
Mother, May I? Even after gaining confidence from losing weight, Victoria still needs her mum's approval on her dress. Meanwhile, Lauren and her mum disagree on styles of gowns. S9, Ep1
Tiffany's Story. Despite a solid support network, Tiffany finds it difficult to break the cycle of depressed eating when her two roommates don't help her. S7, Ep9
Princess Fantasy. Crystal vies for the perfect princess Pnina dress. And, Deborah feels a strong connection with Princess Diana and is determined to have her own Royal Wedding. S9, Ep3
Beat the Clock. Cynthia's veil clashes with her dress causing mayhem, since her wedding is only one month away. Whilst, Passant is running out of time with a limited dress selection. S9, Ep4
Keeping an Open Mind. Tamara is looking for a gown that makes a statement. Meanwhile, Stephanie comes in for her fitting still not convinced that she's bought the right dress. S9, Ep6

Teleshopping.
A Lock-In, A Weather Girl. Sheldon acts as Mary's spy when he's forced to spend the night at church for a youth lock-in. Meanwhile, Georgie gets attracted to an older woman. S5, Ep11
A Pink Cadillac. Sheldon attends his first comic book convention, and Mary tries selling makeup. S5, Ep12
A Lot Of Band-Aids. Sheldon makes friends with his dorm neighbours. Meanwhile, George Sr. learns his job is in jeopardy. S5, Ep13
A Free Scratcher. When a new scientist, Dr. Lee, joins the lab, Sheldon is the odd man out. Meanwhile, Mary is given a lotto ticket. S5, Ep14
A Lobster, An Armadillo. Sheldon joins Dr. Linkletter and Dr. Sturgis on a science road trip, landing them in the middle of nowhere. Georgie continues to lie about his age. S5, Ep15
A Suitcase Full Of Cash. When Meemaw's gambling room is a success, she ends up with a suitcase of illegal cash. Missy starts a business, and Sheldon tries the stock market. S5, Ep16
Some New York Nonsense. Georgie struggles to balance life, work and family. Mandy worries for Georgie's wellbeing and Missy gets into trouble at school. S1, Ep2
Secrets, Lies, Chunk Of Change. Georgie digs into Mandy's past when he finds she's been hiding thousands of dollars of debt. Mandy tries to right her wrongs by going back to work. S1, Ep3
The Space Probe Disintegration. Raj awaits data from a space probe in which he was involved. Later, Leonard and Sheldon go dress shopping with Penny and Amy. S8, Ep12
The Anxiety Optimization. Sheldon becomes concerned that his cushy lifestyle is impacting his professional progress, so he asks the gang to make life more difficult for him. S8, Ep13
The Troll Manifestation. An online troll rips Leonard and Sheldon's physics paper, and a girls' night out leads to Penny, Amy and Bernadette dishing about embarrassing events. S8, Ep14
Comic Book Store Regeneration. Howard gets unsettling news amidst the excitement of the comic book store reopening, and Penny doesn't practice what she preaches. S8, Ep15
The Intimacy Acceleration. An experiment designed to make people fall in love piques Penny and Leonard's interest. Meanwhile, Leonard, Amy, Raj and Emily encounter a 'zombie.' S8, Ep16
The Colonization Application. There's trouble in paradise when Amy learns Sheldon signed up for a one-way mission to colonise Mars. Leonard makes an 'adult' purchase for Penny. S8, Ep17
The Leftover Thermalization. An electrical short thaws the last meal cooked by Mrs. Wolowitz, and Sheldon and Leonard's work is featured in a magazine, but only one gets credit. S8, Ep18
The Skywalker Incursion. Leonard and Sheldon consider dropping by George Lucas' Skywalker Ranch when a speaking engagement puts them nearby. S8, Ep19
Fortification Implementation. Sheldon and Amy reach a crossroad, a man claiming to be Wolowitz's half-brother shows up, and Penny and Leonard argue live on Wil Wheaton's podcast. S8, Ep20
Communication Deterioration. NASA asks Raj to craft a message for aliens in the event of contact, and Penny must choose between an audition or her job in pharmaceutical sales. S8, Ep21
The Graduation Transmission. Wolowitz and Sheldon can't get a drone to fly, Leonard nearly misses giving a commencement address, and Raj pits his parents against each other. S8, Ep22
The Maternal Combustion. Leonard and Sheldon's mothers come to town to celebrate their sons getting an award, but the opinionated women engage in an altercation over religion. S8, Ep23
The Commitment Determination. Leonard and Penny are pressured to set a wedding date by Sheldon, whose relationship with Amy has taken an interesting turn. S8, Ep24
The Matrimonial Momentum. Penny has a problem dealing with Leonard's confession about having kissed another woman, while Sheldon is confused about Amy calling a time out. S9, Ep1
The Separation Oscillation. To ease Penny's mind, Leonard pays a visit to the woman he kissed during his expedition to the North Sea. Sheldon's breakup leads him to retaliate. S9, Ep2
The Bachelor Party Corrosion. The guys surprise Leonard with a belated bachelor-party weekend in Mexico, but their plans hit a bump in the road when they get a flat tire. S9, Ep3
The 2003 Approximation. Sheldon reverts to 2003 when he learns that Leonard and Penny are moving in together, while Howard and Raj form a band to play at the comic store. S9, Ep4
The Perspiration Implementation. When Barry Kripke gives the guys fencing lessons, he makes a point of letting Sheldon know he's interested in dating Amy. S9, Ep5
The Helium Insufficiency. A helium shortage leads Sheldon and Leonard to do business with a dealer in the black market to acquire some of the element for an experiment. S9, Ep6
The Spock Resonance. Sheldon's interview for a 'Star Trek' documentary focusing on Spock turns up a shocking revelation about his breakup with Amy. S9, Ep7

Stourport Basins to Kingswood Junction: Robbie navigates the mighty River Severn and takes an unexpected bath as he takes a tumble at the Tardebigge lock flight in Worcestershire.
Wallace in the Spice Islands: In the Indonesian archipelago the Moluccas, Bill encounters boggle-eyed tarsiers and birds of paradise as he reveals how Wallace cracked evolution.
Desert Worlds: Plants that have developed to thrive in the desert, including cacti that grow in the shade of other trees and collect water in pleated trunks.
Human Worlds: A guide to plants that thrive in human-dominated environments, including trees that grow across canyons in India, which have developed into living bridges.
Citroen / Tractor: The team invest in a piece of French art this week - a 1971 Citroen DS21 Pallas.
The Two Mercs/Fiesta ST: This week tells the tale of the two Mercs, but what will the moral of the story be? Plus, the team get stuck into a moddable favourite - a 2006 Ford Fiesta ST.
Subaru Impreza/Yamaha RD60: The team seek out a sturdy, reliable 4x4 to tackle the rugged Yorkshire landscape in, but get side-tracked into a slightly rusty Subaru Impreza Turbo 2000.
The Death List: The highly esteemed and never bettered political sitcom. Hacker is shocked to learn that his department is responsible for supplying electronic surveillance equipment.
The Greasy Pole: Hacker finds himself in the middle of a major row over the British Chemical Corporation, as Sir Humphrey suggests the politically unpopular measure. Classic laughs.
The Devil You Know: In the acclaimed and hugely influential political sitcom, Jim Hacker is upset by rumours of a cabinet reshuffle and decides to take drastic action for his job.

p.t: War's Secret Shame: Shell Shock with Dan Snow
p.d: New. Historian Dan Snow examines the devastating impact war has on the mental health of soldiers, discovering how First World War shell shock evolved into modern cases of PTSD.
Morris T2/Alfa Romeo Sud: Derek's search for the unusual lands him a 1947 Lea Francis that's half-made of wood. Paul heads for the countryside to pick up a Morris one tonne truck.
Derby to Hinckley: Michael Portillo journeys from the Midlands to the West Country, visiting Derby's famous 19th-century railway works and the Walkers crisps factory in Leicester.
Shopping from Home.
Crewe to Shotton: Michael Portillo visits Crewe, a town steeped in railway history, to investigate the making of cinema classic The Night Mail during the 1930s.
Coventry to Leamington Spa: Michael Portillo hears of the destruction of Coventry's gothic cathedral by the German Luftwaffe, and visits the factory where the London taxi is built.
Plymouth to New London: Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, where he learns about the indigenous tribes of Wampanoag people.
The Source of Iron: Fred Dibnah travels around Britain in style, bringing the great engineers of the past to life. Fred reaches Cumbria where iron ore was once mined on a large scale. Ep3
Castings: Fred Dibnah and his steersman Alf travel up to Scotland, where they marvel at the ingenuity of the Falkirk wheel and visit one of the few surviving traditional iron works. Ep4
Water and Boilers: The great man tours the country, looking at some of our staggering feats of engineering. Fred visits Ryhope pumping station and the Israel Newton boiler works. Ep5
The Road to Steel City: Lancashire's greatest engineering enthusiast travels the country by traction engine. Fred fulfils an ambition by driving across Scammonden Bridge over the M62. Ep6
East: Actor Martin Clunes explores Lord Howe Island, Norfolk Island and Restoration Island.
Martin Clunes travels to the Tiwi Islands, swims with a whale shark, visits the Houtman Abrolhos, and samples life on Rottnest Island.
David Jason examines stories of heroism in the Second World War and explores a world of assassins, saboteurs, commandos, real-life super-villains and the ultimate femmes fatales.
From hi-tech intelligence to undercover ops, David Jason reveals how masterminds of the Second World War defeated Hitler with their problem-solving.
Life in Polar Bear Town: Gordon Buchanan visits Churchill, Manitoba, a Canadian town that for two months of every year is inundated by polar bears making their journey north.

p.t: This World: The Coffee Trail With Simon Reeve
